newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INRO says optimistic of new rubber pact by end '96.
newsitem.headline: INRO says optimistic of new rubber pact by end '96.

text.p: The International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) said on Friday its council of rubber producers and consumers were optimistic of bringing into force before end of 1996 a price pact negotiated since last year.
"Based on the statements made, the council expressed optimism that INRA 1995 (International Natural Rubber Agreement 3) could be brought into force before the end of 1996," INRO said in a statement.

The INRA 3, scheduled to come into force on January 1, 1997, will be the world's only remaining global commodity pact with economic provisions and a buffer stock that allows the industry to buy and sell rubber to stabilise prices.

Its ratification has been held up by Indonesia and Malaysia, two of the world's largest rubber producers, which are both seeking the executive director's post in INRO in exchange for ratifying the agreement. The INRO will govern the new pact.
INRO officials said on Friday that the two countries did not resolve the dispute but added that the council was generally optimistic of ratifying the agreement.
